envelope.text: every subscription DISCOVERED on the topic, matched or not, because

why:
see `c:publisher_get_subscription_count`.

VERDICT (phase-417 gap-verdict pass, 2026-09-21) — ADOPT-BOUNDED, and **THE REASON ABOVE IS FALSE.** It says "We notify on change (`rclc_event_publisher_count_cb_t` + `rclc_count_status_t`)". We do not. That callback carries `NROS_EVENT_LIVELINESS_LOST` and `NROS_EVENT_OFFERED_DEADLINE_MISSED` (`nros_generated.h:2018`), and its subscriber twin carries `REQUESTED_DEADLINE_MISSED` and `MESSAGE_LOST` (`:1967`). There is no `PUBLICATION_MATCHED` / `SUBSCRIPTION_MATCHED` event anywhere in the tree — grep `NROS_EVENT_` and count: five, none of them a match count. A caller keeping "its own mirror of the callback's last value" would be mirroring a different number.

WHAT DOES ANSWER IT is the graph counter phase-381 W4 shipped: `rclc_executor_count_subscribers(executor, topic, out_count)` / `rclc_executor_count_publishers(...)`, in all three languages, over slots Cyclone and zenoh both fill. ADOPT-BOUNDED rather than ADOPT because the two questions differ and the difference must be in the doc comment, not discovered: upstream counts the endpoints MATCHED to THIS entity (QoS-compatible peers of this publisher); the topic-wide count includes an endpoint whose QoS does not match, and on a backend with no QoS negotiation it cannot tell them apart. Weaker, non-inverting, and it answers the use case the row states — skip the work when nobody is listening.

VERDICT (phase-444, 2026-09-22) — DIVERGENCE. **SHIPPED, on rclc's prefix and a weakened signature**, which is what ADOPT-BOUNDED asked for:

  * C: `rclc_publisher_get_subscription_count(publisher, executor, out_count)` and `rclc_subscription_get_publisher_count(subscription, executor, out_count)` (`packages/api/nros-c/src/{publisher,subscription}.rs`, declared in `nros_generated.h`).
  * C++: `Publisher<M>::get_subscription_count(Executor&, size_t*) const` and `Subscription<M>::get_publisher_count(Executor&, size_t*) const`.
  * Rust: `EmbeddedPublisher::get_subscription_count(&Executor)` and `Subscription::get_publisher_count(&Executor)`.

TWO WEAKENINGS, both in the doc comment at every site rather than discovered. (1) THE QUESTION: upstream counts the endpoints MATCHED to THIS entity — peers whose QoS is compatible; we count every endpoint DISCOVERED on the topic, over the graph counter phase-381 W4 shipped. Non-inverting in the SAFE direction: a topic nobody joined still reads `0`, so "skip the work when nobody is listening" — the use this row states — is answered exactly, while an INCOMPATIBLE peer reads `1` where upstream reads `0` (you do work nobody receives, never the reverse). (2) THE RECEIVER: the executor is a parameter, because we open ONE transport session per image and the Executor owns it — the same receiver difference every graph verb carries. Both are what the compiler makes a porter notice, which is RFC-0089's mechanical-edit test.

AND `Unsupported` IS NOT `0`. A backend that cannot read the graph (XRCE) returns an error and does not write the out-parameter; collapsing that into a count would make a caller stop publishing on a backend that simply cannot tell. Pinned by `a_backend_with_no_graph_does_not_report_a_count_of_zero`.

The row stays a `divergence` and not a deletion because the SIGNATURE differs — the correlator files it `differs`, not `same`. On the Rust side the receiver differs too: the key `Publisher` is ours only as `nros_rmw::Publisher`, the RMW seam, and the user handle is `EmbeddedPublisher` (see `rust:Publisher::topic_name` for the same measurement).

CORRECTED 2026-10-25 (phase-515 W0) -- the C bullet above named the pair `rcl_publisher_get_subscription_count` / `rcl_subscription_get_publisher_count`, upstream's spelling. Neither is declared: the shipped names carry the `rclc_` prefix (`nros_generated.h`), because the added `executor` argument makes the contract ours and rcl's name would then bind a three-argument call to rcl's two-argument meaning. Found by the quoted-signature check, which read the old text as rcl's function with one argument too many.
